page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM, translating to 8.0 GB of memory per core. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, the instance allocates 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core on a dedicated basis. The CPU architecture includes a 32 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistent data.

Performance benchmarks position the c2d-highmem-8 as a capable mid-tier performer. It exhibits strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng testing, placing in the top 25% of evaluated instances. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth reaching 62.15 GB/sec for large block read-only operations, and database operations fall within the average range. The instance achieves a Redis SET throughput of 8.97 million operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 10.63 GB/sec. However, LLM inference benchmarks reveal limitations, with prompt processing for a medium 7B model registering in the bottom 25% at 18.65 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highmem-8 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio without the added expense of local NVMe SSDs or GPU accelerators. This resource density makes it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel GPU computing or high-speed local scratch space. Appropriate workloads include relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, medium-scale web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring a larger memory footprint.
